Simulate Data with Calibrated Class Probabilities

Source: R/simulate.R
sim_softcats.Rd

Generates data that satisfy the assumptions of soft_lm(), with options to break them. It is used in the examples, the tests and the vignette.

Usage

sim_softcats(
  n = 2000L,
  K = 2L,
  tau = NULL,
  n_controls = 3L,
  concentration = 5,
  z_effect = 1.5,
  direct_effect = 0,
  miscalibration = 0,
  nonlinear = FALSE,
  labelled_share = 0.2,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n

[optional] (integer) Number of observations (default: 2000).

K

[optional] (integer) Number of categories (default: 2).

tau

[optional] (numeric) Effects of categories 2 to K relative to category 1. NULL uses the first K - 1 values of c(1, -0.5, 0.75, -0.25, 0.5), recycled (default: NULL).

n_controls

[optional] (integer) Number of controls (default: 3).

concentration

[optional] (numeric) Dirichlet concentration; smaller values give more dispersed probabilities and more information beyond the controls (default: 5).

z_effect

[optional] (numeric) Effect of \(Z\) on the class probabilities (default: 1.5).

direct_effect

[optional] (numeric) Direct effect of \(Z\) on the outcome (default: 0).

miscalibration

[optional] (numeric) Strength of the conditional miscalibration of the returned probabilities (default: 0).

nonlinear

[optional] (logical) If TRUE, the outcome regression and the class probabilities are non-linear in the controls (default: FALSE).

labelled_share

[optional] (numeric) Share of observations flagged in column labelled, for use as a labelled sample (default: 0.2).

seed

[optional] (integer) Seed. The random number generator state of the session is restored afterwards (default: NULL).

Value

A data frame with the outcome y, controls x1, x2, ..., the classifier feature z, the latent group group (a factor with levels A, B, ...), probabilities prob_A, prob_B, ... and a logical labelled. Attributes: tau (the true effects), m_true (the true \(E[Y \mid X]\)) and r_true (the true \(E[p \mid X]\) of the calibrated probabilities), computed by Gauss-Hermite quadrature over \(Z\).

Details

The controls \(X\) are independent standard normal variables, and \(Z\) is a standard normal classifier feature that is not a control. Class probabilities are drawn as \(p \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(c\, \pi(X, Z))\), where \(\pi\) is a multinomial logit in \(X\) and \(Z\) and \(c\) is concentration. The group is drawn from \(p\), so the probabilities are calibrated given \(X\) by construction. The outcome is \(Y = \mu(X) + \sum_k \tau_k 1\{G = k\} + \theta Z + \varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon \sim N(0, 1)\) and \(\theta\) = direct_effect.

With miscalibration different from zero, the returned probabilities are distorted: the logit of the second category is shifted by miscalibration * x1, so they are no longer calibrated given \(X\). With direct_effect different from zero, \(Z\) affects the outcome directly and the exclusion restriction fails.

Examples

# Example: Three categories with the true effects
d <- sim_softcats(n = 500, K = 3, seed = 11)
head(d)
#>           y          x1         x2         x3          z group      prob_A
#> 1 1.7535164 -0.59103110  0.9451401 -0.4016787  0.3351174     B 0.229619153
#> 2 0.8110990  0.02659437 -1.3432396 -0.3709327 -1.0826478     B 0.208120303
#> 3 0.3410374 -1.51655310  0.4122123 -0.4251462  1.8231983     B 0.163679508
#> 4 0.2725487 -1.36265335  0.9327749  0.4411515 -0.3771681     C 0.242014817
#> 5 1.1389610  1.17848916 -0.9253432 -0.6727504  1.1349793     B 0.005320046
#> 6 0.8966980 -0.93415132  0.6121816  0.4166941  1.1497207     B 0.491427906
#>       prob_B       prob_C labelled
#> 1 0.63377479 1.366061e-01    FALSE
#> 2 0.09084370 7.010360e-01    FALSE
#> 3 0.76920542 6.711507e-02    FALSE
#> 4 0.03044459 7.275406e-01    FALSE
#> 5 0.99461500 6.495057e-05    FALSE
#> 6 0.50321618 5.355917e-03     TRUE
attr(d, "tau")
#>    B    C 
#>  1.0 -0.5
